chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about what falls into wells. He said: “As for the mouse, water should be drawn out from it until it becomes wholesome. And if a dog falls into it, then if you are able to draw out all that is in it, then do so. And everything that falls into the well that has no blood, such as scorpions, beetles, and the like, then there is no harm.”

key_terms.اَلْآبَارِ: wells; sources of water being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.اَلْبِئْرِ: the well; the specific body of water subject to the ruling
key_terms.اَلْخَنَافِسِ: beetles; another example of creatures without blood in this context
key_terms.اَلْعَقَارِبِ: scorpions; an example of creatures without blood in this context
key_terms.اَلْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse; an animal whose falling into the well requires drawing water out until it becomes wholesome
key_terms.فَيُنْزَحُ: water is to be drawn out; the prescribed action for purifying the well in certain cases
key_terms.كَلْبٌ: a dog; its falling into the well requires emptying the well if one is able
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating no problem in the case of creatures without blood

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on well water if a mouse, dog, or bloodless creature falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings regarding well water when various creatures fall into it. It distinguishes between cases such as a mouse, a dog, and creatures without blood, showing how taharah rulings are applied in practical matters of water purity.
